s: the Saint-Germain café where Sartre and Beauvoir wrote through the war
w: A Saint-Germain-des-Prés institution where Jean-Paul Sartre and Simone de Beauvoir wrote for hours through the winters of the Occupation -- the café had heating when their apartments didn't -- and where Picasso, Camus and a century of Left Bank intellectual life passed through. Still a working café rather than a museum, though the tourists now outnumber the philosophers.
_facts: Located at 172 Boulevard Saint-Germain, 75006 Paris
Opened around 1887; became closely associated with Jean-Paul Sartre and Simone de Beauvoir from the 1930s-40s
Sartre and Beauvoir reportedly worked here through WWII partly because the café was heated
Historic clientele also included Picasso, Apollinaire and Albert Camus

s: a 1926 bistro near Place des Victoires famous for its crème caramel
w: A classic Paris bistro near Place des Victoires, serving since 1926 -- egg mayonnaise, kidneys, sole, onion soup -- with a maître d' ritual regulars come back for as much as the food. The crème caramel, generously portioned and unapologetically old-school, is the dish people specifically return for.
_facts: Located at 1 Rue du Mail, 75002 Paris, near Place des Victoires
Bistro serving classic French cuisine since 1926
Particularly known for its traditional crème caramel dessert
Closed Sunday and Monday

s: a 1927 tea room on Place du Trocadéro famous for melted-bar hot chocolate
w: A Parisian tea room on Place du Trocadéro since 1927, its hot chocolate made by melting down an actual bar of chocolate rather than mixing cocoa powder -- thick, rich, served with whipped cream alongside. Pastries and a view toward the Eiffel Tower make it a long-standing fixture of the 16th arrondissement's genteel café life.
_facts: Located at 4 Place du Trocadéro, 75016 Paris
Founded in 1927 by Jean Carette
Known for its hot chocolate, made from melted chocolate rather than cocoa powder
A short walk from the Eiffel Tower and Trocadéro gardens

s: a matcha-and-brunch café behind a carved stone facade near Saint-Germain
w: Behind a bas-relief-carved facade and leaded windows on Rue des Saints-Pères, a cosy café built around marble bistro tables and exposed beams, best known for its matcha drinks and matcha cheesecake alongside a classic brunch menu. A quiet, considered stop just off Boulevard Saint-Germain.
_facts: Located at 38 Rue des Saints-Pères, 75007 Paris, Saint-Germain-des-Prés
Known for matcha drinks and its signature matcha cheesecake
Also serves coffee, brunch and pastries
Housed behind a decorative carved-stone shop facade

s: a pioneering specialty roaster's Marais branch, known for its cookie pairings
w: One of the branches of Terres de Café, among the earlier specialty coffee roasters to establish itself across Paris, on a quiet street in the Marais. Carefully sourced beans paired with a rotating selection of cookies and pastries chosen specifically to go with the coffee rather than as an afterthought.
_facts: Located at 36 Rue des Blancs-Manteaux, 75004 Paris, Le Marais
One of several Terres de Café locations across Paris
Known as one of the pioneering specialty coffee roasters in the city
Known for cookies and pastries curated to pair with the coffee
